nodes.statement: Computers represent a radical novelty.
nodes.span: the assumption that computers represent a radical novelty.
nodes.status_reason: Stated as an assumption to be explored in the text.

nodes.statement: People typically plan for the future by slightly adapting familiar concepts from their past experience.
nodes.span: we try to get away with the concepts we are familiar with
nodes.status_reason: General observation about human behavior accessible to the reader.

nodes.statement: Relying on past analogies fails when faced with a sharp discontinuity, which is the defining characteristic of a radical novelty.
nodes.span: in the case of a sharp discontinuity, however, the method breaks down
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the definition of radical novelty as a sharp discontinuity where past experience is irrelevant.

nodes.statement: To cope with radical novelty, one must abandon past habits and approach it as an entirely new, disconnected subject.
nodes.span: approach the radical novelty with a blank mind, consciously refusing to try to link it
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the failure of analogies to handle sharp discontinuities.

nodes.statement: People often deny or ignore radical novelties because they find them deeply disturbing.
nodes.span: radical novelties are so disturbing that they tend to be suppressed or ignored
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the hard work and unwelcome nature of adjusting to them.

nodes.statement: Historical examples, such as Gauss hiding his non-Euclidean geometry and the intellectual stagnation of the Middle Ages, show the suppression of novelty.
nodes.span: decided to suppress his discovery of non-Euclidean geometry
nodes.status_reason: Historical anecdotes provided as evidence.

nodes.statement: A surprisingly large portion of people believe that history only progresses through gradual change.
nodes.span: the fraction of the population for which gradual change seems to be all but the only paradigm
nodes.status_reason: Author's personal observation.

nodes.statement: Mathematicians like Herbert Robbins deny the possibility of radical leaps in mathematical ability, insisting the field will remain unchanged.
nodes.span: Robbins flatly refuses to honour any alternative to time-honoured brain usage
nodes.status_reason: Quote and analysis of Robbins provided as an example.

nodes.statement: The education system actively hides novelties by disguising them with familiar, intuitive examples, failing to prepare students for radical change.
nodes.span: They constantly try to present everything that could be an exciting novelty as something as familiar as possible.
nodes.status_reason: Observation of standard educational practices.

nodes.statement: Modern science and technology regularly produce radical novelties that society is poorly equipped to manage.
nodes.span: science and technology have now shown themselves expert at inflicting them upon us.
nodes.status_reason: Supported by historical examples of scientific advancements.

nodes.statement: Automatic computers embody not just one, but two distinct radical novelties.
nodes.span: automatic computers embody not only one radical novelty but two of them.
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the subsequent analysis of computing's properties.

nodes.statement: The first radical novelty of computers is the need to manage unprecedentedly deep conceptual hierarchies due to the massive scale of computing power.
nodes.span: He has to be able to think in terms of conceptual hierarchies that are much deeper
nodes.status_reason: Based on the physical and temporal scales of computing hardware.

nodes.statement: Those who only understand gradual change misunderstand computers by relying on shallow analogies to simpler machines.
nodes.span: the true believer in gradual change and incremental improvements is unable to see it.
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the tendency of gradualists to use shallow analogies.

nodes.statement: The second radical novelty is that computers are discrete digital devices where tiny changes can cause massive effects, unlike familiar continuous analogue mechanisms.
nodes.span: the smallest possible perturbations —i.e. changes of a single bit— can have the most drastic consequences.
nodes.status_reason: Based on the discrete nature of digital information.

nodes.statement: Society denies the discrete, unforgiving nature of computers because accepting it is too uncomfortable.
nodes.span: This second radical novelty shares the usual fate of all radical novelties: it is denied
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the general tendency to deny radical novelties.

nodes.statement: Software engineering is a flawed discipline that attempts to mask the radical novelty of computing by treating it like traditional engineering.
nodes.span: software engineering should be known as "The Doomed Discipline", doomed because it cannot even approach its goal
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the denial of computing's radical novelties.

nodes.statement: The adoption of the title 'software engineer' is a superstitious attempt to make programming seem safe and familiar.
nodes.span: gain some control over some unknown, malicious demon by calling it by a safe, familiar, and innocent name
nodes.status_reason: Observation of industry naming conventions.

nodes.statement: Measuring productivity by lines of code is a misguided practice stemming from the illusion that programs are standard manufactured goods.
nodes.span: measuring "programmer productivity" in terms of "number of lines of code produced per month".
nodes.status_reason: Observation of industry productivity metrics.

nodes.statement: Relying on program testing for quality control ignores the fact that testing cannot prove the absence of bugs in discrete systems.
nodes.span: program testing may convincingly demonstrate the presence of bugs, but can never demonstrate their absence.
nodes.status_reason: Logical property of testing discrete systems.

nodes.statement: The concept of software maintenance relies on the false analogy that abstract programs degrade over time like physical machines.
nodes.span: many people continue to believe that programs —and even programming languages themselves— are subject to wear and tear.
nodes.status_reason: Observation of industry terminology regarding maintenance.

nodes.statement: The push for programming tools is based on a shallow analogy that fails to address the true difficulties of software production.
nodes.span: the suggestion has been accepted that the pains of software production are largely due to a lack of appropriate "programming tools".
nodes.status_reason: Observation of industry reliance on programming tools.

nodes.statement: Artificial Intelligence is embraced because it uses computers to mimic the familiar human mind, thereby hiding the computer's radical novelty.
nodes.span: the frightening computer becomes less frightening if it is used only to simulate a familiar noncomputer.
nodes.status_reason: Author's explanation for the popularity of AI.

nodes.statement: A program is essentially an abstract symbol manipulator that dictates the behavior of a computer.
nodes.span: the program is an abstract symbol manipulator, which can be turned into a concrete one by supplying a computer
nodes.status_reason: Definition of a program in computing science.

nodes.statement: Programs should be viewed as complex mathematical formulae derived through human symbol manipulation.
nodes.span: they look like programs or —to use somewhat more general terminology— usually rather elaborate formulae from some formal system.
nodes.status_reason: Follows from viewing programs as abstract symbol manipulators.

nodes.statement: Computing science is the study of formal methods and symbol manipulation on a massive scale, placing it within formal mathematics and logic.
nodes.span: computing science is —and will always be— concerned with the interplay between mechanized and human symbol manipulation
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the definition of programming as deriving formal formulae.

nodes.statement: Computing science has the potential to fulfill Leibniz's dream by replacing human reasoning with symbolic calculation.
nodes.span: realizing a significant part of Leibniz's Dream of providing symbolic calculation as an alternative to human reasoning.
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the scale and effectiveness of formal methods in computing.

nodes.statement: The vision of computing science as formal mathematics faces widespread opposition from various established groups who refuse to accept its radical nature.
nodes.span: it has met widespread —and sometimes even violent— opposition from all sorts of directions.
nodes.status_reason: List of examples of opposition from various fields.

nodes.statement: Universities fail to teach the rigorous science of computing, instead catering to industry demands and student expectations by dumbing down the curriculum.
nodes.span: The universities will continue to lack the courage to teach hard science, they will continue to misguide the students
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the educational sector's opposition to formal mathematics.

nodes.statement: The term 'bug' should be replaced with 'error' to correctly attribute faults to the programmer rather than an external force.
nodes.span: calling a bug a bug but by calling it an error. It is much more honest because it squarely puts the blame where it belongs
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the need to recognize programmer responsibility.

nodes.statement: Using human-like terms for programs forces people to think about them in terms of their execution over time, which is a paralyzing and wasteful approach.
nodes.span: its adoption effectively prevents a departure from operational semantics and thus forces people to think about programs in terms of computational behaviours
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the mismatch between continuous humans and discrete programs.

nodes.statement: Reasoning about individual computational behaviors is highly inefficient compared to reasoning abstractly using definitions.
nodes.span: if we have to demonstrate something about all the elements of a large set, it is hopelessly inefficient to deal with all the elements
nodes.status_reason: General mathematical principle regarding large sets.

nodes.statement: The mutilated chessboard problem shows that abstract mathematical reasoning is far more powerful and efficient than exhaustively checking all possibilities.
nodes.span: the above simple argument many orders of magnitude shorter than the exhaustive investigation of the possible placements
nodes.status_reason: Mathematical proof provided as an analogy.

nodes.statement: Programmers should analyze programs by examining their text rather than trying to trace their execution.
nodes.span: deal with all computations possible under control of a given program by ignoring them and working with the program.
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the inefficiency of operational reasoning and the power of working with definitions.

nodes.statement: Because programming languages are formal systems, programs should be reasoned about formally, independent of their execution models.
nodes.span: we should reason about programs without even mentioning their possible "behaviours".
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the nature of formal systems.

nodes.statement: Visual educational tools harm students by encouraging them to focus on program execution rather than formal reasoning.
nodes.span: they were used to display all sorts of features of computations evolving under control of the student's program!
nodes.status_reason: Observation of a specific educational tool.

nodes.statement: A programmer's true task is to mathematically prove that a program satisfies its formal functional specification.
nodes.span: The programmer's task is to present such complete conjectures as proven theorems.
nodes.status_reason: Follows from viewing programs as formal formulae.

nodes.statement: A proper introductory programming course should teach formal logic and a clean programming language, requiring students to mathematically prove their programs correct without ever executing them.
nodes.span: the programming language in question has not been implemented on campus so that students are protected from the temptation to test their programs.
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the need to ban operational reasoning and enforce formal mathematical derivation.

nodes.statement: The proposed formal programming course is practically viable, having been successfully taught to many freshmen for years.
nodes.span: since the early 80's, such an introductory programming course has successfully been given to hundreds of college freshmen each year.
nodes.status_reason: Empirical evidence from the author's teaching experience.

nodes.statement: Teaching formal methods provides students with immense intellectual power and confidence, fulfilling the university's duty to embrace radical novelties.
nodes.span: Teaching to unsuspecting youngsters the effective use of formal methods is one of the joys of life because it is so extremely rewarding.
nodes.status_reason: Follows from the success of the proposed course and the power of formal methods.
